newsitem.title: CHILE: ABN-AMRO approves $175 mln loan to Chile utility.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO approves $175 mln loan to Chile utility.

text.p: The Chilean division of Dutch bank ABN-AMRO Bank has approved a $175 million loan to Chilean electricity utility Colbun SA, which will be used to finance the firm's expansion plans, said an official.
"It's a seven-year syndicated loan with two-year grace period," Nayib Bendeck, account executive for Colbun, told Reuters.
Bendeck said the authorization letter for the loan has already been signed by the bank, although Colbun has yet to receive the funds.

Colbun, which was privatized last year, plans to invest $450 million in coming years to beef up its generating capacity and consolidate its position as the third largest power generator in Chile's central grid.
Projects include a gas-fired power plant in the central Fifth Region, a hydro-electric project, and an electricity transmission line.
Colbun is controlled by the Inversora Andina - Minera Valparaiso group, which bought 37.5 percent of the company for $341 million last year.
Inversora Andina includes Belgium's Powerfin POWE.BR, Spanish firm Iberdrola, and Chile's Enagas.
